title: BZK09 §2.1 adaptive mixed-integer solver in MiGreedyRounding
description:
BLOCKER for PATCH-98: our MiGreedyRounding does a full sparse Cholesky-class decompose every iteration, taking minutes on 20K-face rocker-arm. BZK09 section 2.1 line 137-160 describes their adaptive algorithm: After each integer rounding, push the affected variables nonzero(A_i) into a queue and run local Gauss-Seidel. If GS does not converge within maxiter, fall back to global Conjugate Gradient. If CG also fails, fall back to sparse Cholesky. The doc on FaceRosyField explicitly notes 'Adequate for meshes up to ~10k faces. Beyond that, pattern-preserving refactor or a CHOLMOD-class solver becomes necessary.' Lyon's pipeline relies on the adaptive solver to handle larger inputs (BRAIN model has 100k faces, 3721 sing in their Table 1). Implementation: add Gauss-Seidel pass over a push-queue of dependent variables after each chord pin, before falling back to current full-decompose path.

UPDATE 2026-05-01: First-cut implementation landed but vanilla GS path is too slow to be useful.

WHAT LANDED:
- MiGreedyRounding now builds CSR-style adjacency once via buildAdjacency() (rowStart, rowCol, rowVal, diag, baseRhs).
- tryLocalGS(pinnedChord, value) implements BZK09 Algorithm 1 over the maintained currentX. Handles directional constraints (PATCH-96) and gauge as exact pins.
- Stats exposed: statGsConverged, statGsFellBack, statGsTotalIters.
- Made class public + stats public for benchmark visibility.
- Default behavior: GS path DISABLED (vanilla GS converges too slowly per pin to beat direct re-decompose).
- Opt-in via -Dixdar.bzk09.useGs=true for A/B testing.

EMPIRICAL: vanilla GS on level-4 sphere (2048 faces, 6000 vars) takes 5000+ iters per pin and never falls back, total runtime exceeds full sparse re-decompose. BZK09 paper notes this in section 2.1: pure iterative is generally NOT enough — they specifically use CG fallback for medium-difficulty pins. Without CG, GS-only is slower than direct.

REMAINING WORK:
- Add Conjugate Gradient fallback (BZK09 section 2.1 line 178-181). CG converges in O(sqrt(condition_number)) iters for SPD systems, much faster than GS.
- Test ladder: GS for small pins -> CG for medium -> sparse Cholesky for hard.
- ojAlgo may have CG built in worth checking.

Once CG fallback lands, the adaptive solver becomes net-positive and PATCH-98 can wire it through to recompute the rocker-arm cross-field.

PATCH-97 STATUS: infrastructure shipped, default-off pending CG. 92/92 regression green.


UPDATE 2026-05-01 (round 2): CG fallback shipped, gives 24x speedup on level-3 sphere.

WHAT LANDED:
- tryCG(newlyPinnedChord, pinValue) implements Conjugate Gradient on the unpinned subspace, warm-started from currentX. Pinned set unifies gauge θ[0]=0, directional constraints, chord pins. Effective RHS computed by substitution.
- Solver ladder: GS (opt-in, default off) -> CG (default on) -> sparse direct (final fallback).
- Stats exposed: statCgConverged, statCgFellBack, statCgTotalIters.
- BenchmarkRockerArmLyon flag -Dixdar.lyon.recomputeField=true triggers FaceRosyField recompute (PATCH-98 wiring).

PERF MEASUREMENT:
- subdividedSphereEulerCharacteristicHolds (level-3 sphere, 512 faces): 17.05s -> 0.72s = 24x speedup with CG.
- 92/92 quadlayout regression green.

REMAINING: scaling limit observed. Tests on level-5 sphere (8192 faces) and rocker-arm (20088 faces) still take more than 5 minutes. CG iterations per pin scale with sqrt(condition_number) of the LSE matrix. For larger meshes, condition number grows, requiring more iterations. Possible next steps (separate ticket):
- Preconditioned CG (Jacobi or block-diagonal preconditioner)
- Incremental factorization update instead of full re-decompose for sparse Cholesky path
- Reduce CG_MAX_ITER and accept lower-accuracy solutions for bulk of pins

PATCH-97 STATUS: CG ladder shipped, 24x faster on small meshes, but rocker-arm-scale meshes still need more perf work. The infrastructure (CSR adjacency, GS, CG, fallback to direct) is in place.
definition-of-done: MiGreedyRounding completes in under 30 seconds on the rocker-arm 20K-face mesh. Each pin operation primarily uses local Gauss-Seidel; CG fallback when GS does not converge; sparse Cholesky only as last resort. Singularity count and energy match the previous full-decompose impl on small meshes (cube, sphere) within machine precision tolerance. Quadlayout regression green.
testing-plan: 1) Implement local Gauss-Seidel update on push-set of variables affected by each pin. 2) Add CG fallback. 3) Keep current sparse decompose as final fallback. 4) Verify on subdivided sphere (existing tests) that result matches old impl. 5) Run on rocker-arm and time the full FaceRosyField solve.
